nodes.label: @workspace/ui Package
nodes.rationale: Components are generated into packages/ui/src/components and imported by every app so the design system has a single source of truth across web and admin.

nodes.label: Counter-Action Pairing
nodes.rationale: Each attack names the defense that counters it and vice versa, so the resolution engine can look up the opposing action symmetrically from either side of an exchange.

nodes.label: Success Probability Model (0-100 percent)
nodes.rationale: Probabilities are authored as percentages for human-readable configuration and converted to 0-1 internally at evaluation time, keeping config ergonomics separate from math.

nodes.label: POST /admin/configure_all
nodes.rationale: A single configure_all call sets sides, teams, players, actions, factors, credits and black-market inventory at once so the game can never be started from a partially initialized configuration.

nodes.label: Configuration Coherence Constraints
nodes.rationale: Side/team names are case-sensitive keys in mapping objects and undefined teams or sides cause validation or runtime errors, so coherence across side_names, team_names, side_assignments and actions must be checked before start_game.

nodes.label: Nash Equilibrium Analytics
nodes.rationale: NE analytics run asynchronously and are never exposed via API or the info socket, so strategy evaluation informs admins without becoming an in-game oracle for players.

nodes.label: Per-Turn NE Plot Output
nodes.rationale: Verbose matrix and per-target text logs are disabled in favor of rendered plot tables, because per-turn matrices are unreadable as text at game scale.

nodes.label: SAS Composite Score (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: SAS was dropped from the latest calculation in favor of the payoff matrix and EV alone; ev_weight and progress_weight are still computed but unused, so they must not be treated as live tuning knobs.

nodes.label: Modifier Types (increase / decrease / multiply)
nodes.rationale: Splitting additive deltas from multiplicative factors lets a single value field drive very different balance levers (flat probability points vs. scaling growth) without adding new event shapes.

nodes.label: Black Market Economy
nodes.rationale: Black-market inventory is fixed at configure_all time and purchased in-game by team vote, so the item pool is an admin balance decision while spending it is a player strategy decision.

nodes.label: Points Scoring (1 point per successful attack)
nodes.norm_label: points scoring (1 point per successful attack)

nodes.label: Vote Weight and Leader Flag
nodes.rationale: Weighted votes plus an is_leader flag let a team break ties and express hierarchy without changing the voting protocol itself.

nodes.label: WebSocket /ws/game-info Observer Channel
nodes.rationale: The observer channel deliberately withholds NE analytics so spectators and admin dashboards cannot leak strategy-quality information back to players.

nodes.label: Per-Turn Resolution Loop
nodes.rationale: A fixed per-turn ordering (effects -> notify -> collect votes -> resolve purchases/actions -> persist -> async analytics) makes turn outcomes deterministic and auditable, and keeps expensive NE analytics off the critical path of gameplay.

nodes.label: status + currentPhase Gameplay Gating
nodes.rationale: Gameplay must be gated on status plus currentPhase; the coarse phase field only describes lifecycle and is too blunt to drive UI enablement.

nodes.label: Limit Effects (disable_attack / disable_defense)
nodes.rationale: Limit events override action availability irrespective of probabilities, giving admins a hard on/off lever that cannot be defeated by accumulated buffs.

nodes.label: Attacker-Specific Vulnerability Tracking
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities are keyed by attacker and action so a successful breach rewards the specific attacker with higher future success, while a successful defense clears only that attacker's foothold rather than globally resetting the target.

nodes.label: Player Connection Code
nodes.rationale: Codes are server-generated per player so a player's WebSocket identity cannot be spoofed by guessing a display name, and so configuration fully precedes connection.

nodes.label: SSE Event Stream /api/games/{gameId}/events/stream
nodes.rationale: Readiness is signalled by connecting to the SSE stream because this contract has no /client/connect endpoint to handshake against.

nodes.label: userId Player Identity
nodes.rationale: Player identity is userId only; clients must not depend on a separate public playerId because the contract does not guarantee one.
